title: Why South Asian BMI and waist cutoffs are stricter
summary: Indian consensus uses BMI >=23 for overweight and >=25 for obesity (instead of 25/30) because South Asians carry higher visceral fat at lower body weights.
answer: Indian Consensus Guidelines (Misra et al.) define BMI 18.5-22.9 kg/m2 as normal, 23.0-24.9 as overweight, and >=25.0 as obese. Central obesity is flagged at waist >=90 cm for men and >=80 cm for women because abdominal visceral fat drives insulin resistance, fatty liver, and early cardiovascular risk even at modest BMI.

title: How the Indian Diabetes Risk Score (IDRS) works
summary: MDRF IDRS scores 0-100 from four simple inputs: age

column8: IDRS (<30 Low, 30-59 Moderate, >=60 High) is a validated Indian screening tool (Mohan et al.). An IDRS >=60 detects undiagnosed diabetes and prediabetes with high sensitivity and should be followed up with a fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and HbA1c lab test.

title: Understanding CKD-EPI 2021 eGFR and Urine ACR
summary: CKD-EPI 2021 estimates kidney filtration without race adjustment; pairing eGFR with Urine ACR catches early diabetic or hypertensive kidney strain.
answer: Kidney risk uses both eGFR (G1 >=90, G2 60-89, G3a 45-59, G3b 30-44, G4 15-29, G5 <15 mL/min/1.73m2) and Urine ACR (A1 <30, A2 30-300, A3 >300 mg/g). Even with eGFR >=90, an ACR >=30 mg/g indicates early kidney stress that responds well to BP and sugar control.

column7: Replace polished white rice or maida rotis with mixed-grain roti (jowar, bajra, ragi, whole wheat) or hand-pounded brown rice. Limit cooking oil to 3-4 teaspoons/day, avoid vanaspati/reused frying oil, keep salt under 5 g/day (1 tsp), and pair every meal with dal/sprouts and high-fiber vegetables.

column7: Avoid adding table salt, pickles (achaar), papad, and packaged namkeen. Include potassium-rich whole foods (spinach, lauki, banana, coconut water unless potassium-restricted for advanced CKD) and walk briskly 30 minutes daily after medical clearance.

column7: If you have High risk BP (>=140/90), high 10-year CVD risk, or uncontrolled diabetes, avoid heavy isometric straining or sudden high-intensity sprints until cleared by a physician. Start with 15-20 minutes of flat, conversational-pace walking and gentle stretching.

column7: Never discontinue blood pressure tablets, statins, or diabetes medications when numbers look normal—normal readings mean the medicine is working. Use a weekly pill organizer or phone alarm, and bring all prescriptions to every follow-up visit.

Call 112 or 108 immediately.

title: Reversing metabolic fatty liver (MASLD) early
summary: Losing 5-7% body weight

tags: and brisk walking significantly reduce liver fat within 3-6 months.
column7: Fatty liver commonly co-exists with central obesity, high triglycerides, and prediabetes. Eliminate sugar-sweetened beverages, fruit juices, and alcohol; prioritize dal, paneer/tofu, leafy greens, and 150+ min/week moderate aerobic exercise. Ask your doctor if FibroScan is needed.

title: Stopping tobacco lowers heart and stroke risk rapidly
summary: Within 1 year of quitting smoking
answer: excess coronary heart disease risk drops by roughly half.
tags: Every cigarette or bidi accelerates arterial plaque and doubles stroke/MI risk. Use a verified smoking cessation clinic, nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) if advised by a doctor, and behavioral triggers tracking.

title: How brisk walking lowers blood sugar and BP
summary: 30 minutes of brisk walking daily improves insulin uptake for up to 24 hours and lowers systolic BP by 4-8 mmHg.
answer: Walking recruits large leg muscles that absorb glucose even with lower insulin levels. Aim for 30-45 minutes on 5+ days/week at a pace where you can talk in short sentences without gasping.

title: Why a 10-minute walk after meals works so well
summary: Walking gently for 10-15 minutes after lunch and dinner blunts post-meal blood sugar spikes by 15-25%.
answer: Post-prandial glucose peaks 45-90 minutes after eating. A light stroll right after meals uses that circulating glucose directly in leg muscles and reduces strain on the pancreas.

title: Safe strength training for diabetes and metabolic syndrome
summary: Twice-weekly bodyweight or resistance-band exercises (chair squats, wall push-ups) build muscle that burns glucose at rest.
answer: Muscle tissue is the largest glucose reservoir in the body. Perform 2 sets of 10-12 controlled reps twice a week while exhaling during effort—never hold your breath (Valsalva) if you have high BP.

title: Pranayama and yoga poses safe for hypertension
summary: Slow nasal breathing (Anulom Vilom, Bhramari) and Shavasana lower stress hormones and resting blood pressure.
answer: Avoid forceful breath-holding (kumbhaka) or head-down inversions if BP is >=140/90. Stick to gentle seated pranayama, Shavasana, Setu Bandhasana, and Chair Yoga.

title: Exercise rules when Stage 2 BP or High CVD risk is flagged
summary: Do not start vigorous running or heavy weights without a physician checkup; begin with conversational-pace flat walking.
answer: If your BP is >=140/90 or WHO CVD risk is >=20%, sudden intense exertion can spike blood pressure. Start with 15-20 minutes of flat walking and ask your doctor about a TMT or ECG clearance.

title: Diabetic foot safety before and after exercise
summary: Wear cushioned, seamless socks and well-fitted walking shoes; inspect feet daily for blisters or redness.
answer: Neuropathy can hide minor shoe friction. Check both feet after every walk, keep nails trimmed straight, and never walk barefoot outdoors.

title: Which hospitals have 24x7 Cath Lab and Cardiac ICU?
summary: Verified tertiary centers like AIIMS, KEM, PGIMER, CMC Vellore, Apollo, Fortis Escorts, Medanta, Narayana, SCTIMST, and Jupiter provide 24x7 cath lab care.
answer: In an acute heart attack, door-to-balloon angioplasty within 90 minutes saves heart muscle. Always confirm 24x7 cath lab and emergency triage availability.

title: Accessing dialysis and CKD care at verified hospitals
summary: Public and empaneled hospitals (AIIMS, KEM, PGIMER, NIMS, SSKM, Apollo, Medanta, KIMS, DMCH) offer dialysis and nephrology clinics.
answer: Check whether the hospital has a PMJAY / CGHS desk for subsidized or cashless maintenance hemodialysis and regular eGFR/electrolyte monitoring.

title: What happens in a hospital Cardiac Rehabilitation program?
summary: Supervised 8-12 week programs combine ECG-monitored exercise, Indian dietitian counseling, and stress management.
answer: Cardiac rehab lowers repeat heart events and hospitalizations. Hospitals such as CMC Vellore, Fortis Escorts, Medanta, Kokilaben, Narayana, and SCTIMST run structured rehab clinics.

title: Government health schemes: PMJAY, CGHS, MJPJAY, Chiranjeevi & Aarogyasri
summary: Public and empaneled hospitals across states accept Ayushman Bharat (PMJAY), CGHS, MJPJAY (Maharashtra), CMCHIS (Tamil Nadu), Aarogyasri (AP/TS), and Swasthya Sathi (WB).
answer: Carry your Aadhaar/ABHA ID, scheme card, and prior lab reports to the hospital insurance desk before admission or planned procedures.

title: What to bring to your cardiology or diabetes OPD visit
summary: Bring 7-day home BP/sugar logs, all current medicine strips, and recent HbA1c, lipid, and creatinine reports.
answer: Organized records save repeat blood draws and help your specialist adjust doses safely in one visit.

title: Hydration rules during exercise in kidney disease vs healthy adults
summary: Most adults should drink water before and after walks; CKD Stage 3b-5 patients should follow their nephrologist fluid limit.
answer: If you have normal kidney function, hydrate well especially in Indian summers. If you have advanced CKD or heart failure with fluid restriction, follow your prescribed daily fluid allowance.

title: How to break sitting time at a desk job
summary: Stand and walk for 3 minutes every 45 minutes of sitting to prevent post-meal lipid and glucose spikes.
answer: Even regular gym-goers suffer metabolic slowdown if they sit 8+ hours straight. Pair hourly 3-minute walks with neck/shoulder rolls.

title: Linking lab reports with your ABHA (ABDM) Health ID
summary: ABHA lets you store and share digital lab results across AIIMS and verified private hospitals without losing paper copies.
answer: Ask the hospital ABDM desk or use an ABDM-enabled app to link your ECG, HbA1c, and creatinine history.

title: Minimum weekly target vs optimal weekly target
summary: WHO & ICMR recommend at least 150 minutes/week of moderate aerobic activity plus 2 days of muscle strengthening.
answer: Even 10-minute blocks add up! Consistency 5 days a week matters far more than one exhausting weekend session.
